Algorithmic settings for the contamination-mixture samplers

Source: R/priors.R
mixture_control.Rd

Algorithmic settings for the contamination-mixture samplers

Usage

mixture_control(
  c_infl = NULL,
  pg_terms = 128L,
  irls_steps = 3L,
  m1_update = c("exact", "original")
)

Arguments

c_infl

Variance-inflation factor \(c > 1\) of the covariate density of contaminated observations in model "Mjoint": good observations have \(x \sim N(\hat\mu_P, \hat\Sigma_P)\), contaminated ones \(x \sim N(\hat\mu_P, c\,\hat\Sigma_P)\). NULL (default) uses the family-specific default of the original code: 4 for Gaussian, 2.5 for binomial and Poisson.

pg_terms

Number of terms \(K\) in the truncated sum-of-gammas representation used to draw Polya-Gamma variables (binomial family). Default 128, as in the original code.

irls_steps

Number of Newton (IRLS) steps used to locate the conditional mode for the Laplace proposal of the Poisson coefficient update. Default 3, as in the original code. Larger values make the independence Metropolis-Hastings step closer to exact (see Details in mixture_fit()).

m1_update

How the rival-regression component of model "M1" is updated when few observations are allocated to it. "exact" (default) always uses the correct full conditional given the allocated observations (a proper prior makes this well defined for any number of observations). "original" reproduces the original code, which draws \(\beta_{bad}\) from its prior whenever \(\le p + 1\) observations are allocated to the contaminated component; this ignores those observations and is not a valid Gibbs step, so it is provided only for reproducing earlier results.

Value

An object of class bsm_control.

Examples

mixture_control(c_infl = 3)
#> $c_infl
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $pg_terms
#> [1] 128
#> 
#> $irls_steps
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $m1_update
#> [1] "exact"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "bsm_control"
